answer: The system binds each identity to one hardware key sealed around a single onyx bead, and enrollment records the key signature plus the bead's weight to 0.1 gram, so a copied key without that exact bead fails. That key then completes a voyage of at least 500 kilometers over at least 7 days, ending at a harbor where its fresh signature is scanned, and earns no weight until the arrival scan matches its departure scan. Each fake needs its own key, its own bead, and its own 7-day voyage, because one key can be in only one place at a time.
